title: Longest Run With at Most K Kinds
statement:
You get a string s and a number k. Return the length of the longest contiguous piece of s that uses at most k different characters.

If k is 0, no character is allowed, so the answer is 0.

examples.why: "accc" uses only a and c. "aba" also has 2 kinds but is shorter.
"xyx" is the best. Picking x and y from the whole string gives x, y, x, y, x (5), but those letters are not contiguous.
k may exceed the number of kinds in the string; then the whole string fits.

hints: Fix the left end of the piece and extend it to the right until a (k+1)-th kind appears. Can the next left end reuse that work?
Keep a window [left, right] and a count of each character inside it. The number of keys with a positive count is the number of kinds.
Grow right by one each step. While the window has more than k kinds, drop s[left] and move left. Record the window size after each step.

explain.intuition:
If a window has at most k kinds, every smaller window inside it does too. So when adding a character pushes the count to k + 1, no window with the current left end can ever work again, and the left end can only move right. Both ends move forward only, which is the sliding-window shape.

A map from character to count tells you how many kinds are inside. When a count drops to zero, delete the key, so the map's size is the number of kinds.
steps: While count has more than k keys, decrease the count of s[left], delete it if it hits 0, and move left right.
pitfalls: Counting kinds across the whole string instead of contiguous pieces, as in "xyxzyx".
Leaving zero-count keys in the map, so its size overstates the kinds and the window shrinks too much.
Not handling k = 0: the shrink loop must empty the window, giving 0.

solutions.title: Every start, extend until too many kinds
solutions.idea: For each left end, extend right with a set of kinds until a (k+1)-th kind appears.

solutions.title: Sliding window with counts
solutions.idea: Grow the right end; while the window has more than k kinds, shrink from the left.

followups: The string arrives as a stream and you can't store it. Keep only the last index of each character in the window. How do you find which one to evict?
Count the pieces with exactly k kinds instead of finding the longest. (Hint: at most k minus at most k − 1.)
